load_basis: 2024 ANNUAL AVERAGE, not a 2025 figure: Meta's 2025 Environmental Data Index reports 865,803 MWh of electricity consumed at Huntsville (AL) in calendar 2024; divided by 8,784 hours = 98.6 MW average whole-facility draw (includes cooling and overhead, so it is not IT capacity). 2025 consumption had not been published when this was compiled (no 2026 index on Meta's site as of 2026-11-11). Prior years from the same table: 2021 85,286 MWh; 2022 368,841 MWh (42.1 MW avg); 2023 614,198 MWh (70.1 MW avg). The site grew about 41% from 2023 to 2024, so the 2025 average is probably higher than 98.6 MW; treat this as a floor.
notes: SAME CAMPUS as known fids bi:8-0, osm:way/1160814413, osm:way/1540172608, osm:way/1540172612 and epoch:Meta Huntsville: one Meta campus in North Huntsville Industrial Park; merge, do not sum. Arrangement entered as retail through the local power company; whether a TVA large-load contract sits behind it was not established. Coordinates are from OSM way 1160814413 (already in our inventory); no street address was retrieved. Buildout MW left null: no primary source. Meta's info sheet gives $1.5B+ invested and a 2018 groundbreaking.

site_name: Google Jackson County Data Center (Widows Creek, Bridgeport)
notes: SAME CAMPUS as known fids bi:1302-0, osm:way/714889192, osm:way/844371952 and osm:way/844371953: one Google campus on TVA's former Widows Creek coal plant site; merge, do not sum. LOAD NOT FOUND: no Google, TVA or regulator document giving this campus's MW or MWh was retrieved; Google does not publish per-site electricity use. This is the largest unsized site in the state. The MW figures in press coverage are generation contracts, not site load (about 300 MW of solar contracted with TVA in 2019 for the Alabama and Tennessee data centers; up to 50 MW from Kairos Hermes 2 for Google sites in Alabama and Tennessee). Utility: Area Development (25 Jun 2015) reports 'TVA also directly serves large Alabama industrial customers and government facilities. Google will bring the total of direct-served customers to 12.' That is an announcement-era statement; no later document confirming direct service was retrieved (TVA's NEPA page for the Widows Creek switching station and transmission connections refused automated access), hence medium. TVA direct service is entered as wholesale_direct: the customer buys from TVA itself and its load does not pass through a local power company's retail sales (North Alabama Electric Cooperative is the surrounding distributor and was not named in any source). Start year: sources conflict. Google's site page (https://datacenters.google/locations/jackson-county-alabama/) lists both groundbreaking and opening under 2018; Alabama Reporter and 256 Today (June 2026) say announced 2018, operating 2019; Data Center Knowledge described it as under construction on 18 Jan 2019. 2019 used. Our bi:1302-0 start year of 2022 is not supported by any of these. A $1.5B expansion through 2027 was announced June 2026. Coordinates are from OSM way 714889192; no street address was retrieved.

site_name: Digi Power X (formerly Digihost) Columbiana facility
operator: Digi Power X Inc. (formerly Digihost Technology; US Data Centers subsidiary)
load_basis: CAPACITY, NOT A FULL-YEAR 2025 LOAD. The company's FY2024 annual report (Form 20-F filed 31 Mar 2025) describes the Alabama site as 'a 22 MW utility powered site with an operating hashrate of 500 PH' (bitcoin mining). Its FY2025 Form 10-K says mining-related costs at the Alabama site 'were minimized from April 2025 through the end of the year' while the site was converted to a Tier III AI data center, and the first AI pod was not expected to be fully active until Q2 2026. So the site ran at up to about 22 MW in January to March 2025 and at a small, unpublished load for the rest of 2025. If a 2025 annual average is needed, an upper bound is about 5.5 MW (22 MW x 3/12); that is arithmetic on the filings, not a company figure.
notes: Not in our inventory (new site). Bitcoin mine through early 2025, now being converted to AI/HPC colocation, so label it crypto for 2022 to 2025 and colocation from 2026. Address 130 Industrial Parkway, Columbiana, AL (Form 10-K, Item 1/2); coordinates from the U.S. Census geocoder for that address (matched '130 INDUSTRIAL PKWY, COLUMBIANA, AL, 35051', Shelby County). Property acquired 14 Jun 2022, about 160,000 sq ft, 'initial access to 28 MW of power with a total capacity of up to 55 MW'. First 100 PH of mining came online December 2022 (FY2022 Form 20-F). Utility: the FY2022 20-F says the company moved miners to Alabama 'to benefit from the lower direct energy costs it has negotiated with Alabama Power' and posted a $1.3 million surety bond 'with Alabama Power Company for electric service'. special_contract is my reading of 'negotiated'; no Alabama PSC contract filing was retrieved, so the arrangement could instead be a standard large-customer tariff option. Buildout: 10-K lists 'Alabama site: 55 MW' power available, with 40 MW critical load planned by Q4 2026; the same filing elsewhere says 70 MW secured in Alabama after a further load study. Press reports (not opened: DatacenterDynamics refused automated access) describe a 40 MW agreement with Cerebras, Phase 1 of 15 MW IT expected December 2026. For the EPRI 2024 comparison this site was running as a roughly 22 MW mine throughout 2024.

site_name: Core Scientific Auburn (former AUBix data center)
load_basis: No operating load published. Core Scientific's FY2025 Form 10-K lists 50 MW of 'gross utility power capacity' at Auburn, Alabama from Alabama Power Company as of 31 Dec 2025, and says only that 'a portion' of its ten facilities were operating at that date with the rest under construction or development; it does not say which. The February 2025 company release said the site 'will launch with a capacity of 16 megawatts'. Neither is evidence of load actually drawn in 2025.
notes: Not in our inventory (new site). Included because it has 50 MW of utility capacity on the books at end-2025, but whether it drew 10 MW or more in 2025 is NOT established; do not count load until a source says so. Address 1571 W Samford Ave, Auburn, AL (Core Scientific press release, Feb 2025), inside the existing AUBix building (40,000 sq ft on 5.7 acres per trade press). Coordinates left null: the U.S. Census geocoder returned no match for the West Samford address (it matched East Samford, which is the wrong location). The AUBix building predates Core Scientific as a small colocation site; its original opening year was not retrieved, and Core's lease was reported to begin November 2024. planned_full_buildout_mw is the 10-K gross utility capacity (50 MW), not critical IT; initial launch capacity 16 MW. Service arrangement unknown: the 10-K describes its supply contracts generically as 'fixed, variable and interruptible bi-lateral power supply consumption agreements'.
